doc.title: Spiegle Willcox and Al Gallodoro interviewed by Monk Rowe, Norwich, New York, November 14, 1995

title: What the word jazz meant in the twenties
summary: Gallodoro and Willcox say jazz meant improvised Dixieland, alongside sweet popular tunes like Whispering, and mention Bill Challis with Whiteman.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: What the word "jazz" means: origins, Dixieland and labels

blocks.x: The word “jazz” at this time, did it have a different meaning than it does now? I mean you had the jazz age, and did jazz mean all popular music at that time?
That you improvised on. Like Dixieland. It’s all jazz. Like “Struttin’ With Some Barbecue” [scats].
It seems like the popular music of the day was jazz oriented. Is that right?
Yeah, but you had sweet tunes also. Like “Whispering” that Paul Whiteman made famous. Oh, God, so many beautiful tunes.
Of course we had Bill Challis, Bill was with Whiteman then of course.
That’s right. I knew Bill from New York.
